text:
cheng: Heads-up — saw ~2.8x p99 latency spike on runtime-rtg-7 while serving very long chats (>8k tokens). Correlates with aggressive KV evictions and a burst of reinserts. Putting initial notes here.

maria: Oof. Any logs or flamegraphs?

cheng: Pasting a small evicter log snippet we captured on canary:```
[evicter] ts=3400012330 shard=3 action=evict entries=128 scan_len=1024 reinserts=18 hold_ms=12
[request] ts=3400012331 id=req-9f2 gen=kv-get miss=true
[evicter] ts=3400012332 shard=3 action=evict entries=256 scan_len=2048 reinserts=34 hold_ms=45
[request] ts=3400012333 id=req-9f3 wait_on_lock=true
```
That "hold_ms=45" line repeats during the spike.

alex: I think that's the lock contention we talked about — reinserts trigger a path that takes the global slab lock and blocks request threads. Under steady state that's fine, but with long contexts the hotset oscillates and reinserts go up.

sanjay: Are we running FIFO reinsert logic or LRU sampling there? FIFO reinserts can cause the scan to walk the whole page more often under churn.

cheng: Canary is set to LRU sampling, but there's a fallback to FIFO heuristic when we detect lots of sequential allocations. We didn't flip anything recently AFAIK.

maria: Last week's kernel selection change bumped per-kv-entry metadata (extra tag for quantized kernels). Could that increase memory so paging triggers earlier?

cheng: Possible. The per-entry footprint went from ~56B to ~72B in that build. Increased occupancy -> more frequent evicts -> more reinserts -> contention.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T10:02 - rolled canary (runtime-rtg-7) with candidate runtime v2.9.4-quant-kernel.

samir: Quick repro idea: run long-context loop with 12k token prefix, emit many unique prefixes to maximize hotset churn, watch evicter scan_len and reinserts. I can script this.

alex: Good. In the meantime we should mitigate: (1) avoid taking the global slab lock during reinserts (make reinserts per-shard or lock-free), (2) batch reinserts so evicter does a single batch op, (3) add upper bound on scan_len with backoff.

maria: Also add telemetry: histogram of reinserts_per_evict, evicter_hold_ms, and scan_len_percentile. Right now we only log entries_evicted which doesn't tell the whole story.

sanjay: For correctness: confirm FIFO fallback doesn't violate pointer invariants during concurrent reinserts. We saw a rare stale-pointer assert in debug a few weeks ago.

cheng: I ran the debug build and repro'd a stale pointer once; looks like reinsertion can race with pager reclamation when the page is being compacted. Not seen on non-FIFO in my runs.

alex: That suggests FIFO's reinsertion order increases window where a tombstone or moved entry is referenced. If so, correctness fix is higher priority than perf.

samir: I'll instrument a light-weight sampler to capture reinserts + pager compaction overlap. If we can reproduce reliably we can write a unit test and patch the reinsertion handshake.

maria: Short-term mitigation: flip canary back to non-quant kernel (rollback) and throttle evicter under heavy reinserts. We can deploy a config flag to increase eviction cooldown.

cheng: I pushed a tiny patch that caps scan_len to 512 and adds a 1ms backoff before subsequent evicts. Canary running with that now.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T10:14 - rolled canary (runtime-rtg-7) with evicter-cap-scan_len=512.

alex: Keep an eye on p50/p95/p99. If the cap reduces p99 but increases memory pressure we still need the better fix.

maria: I'll add the telemetry and a Grafana panel for reinserts/hold_ms. Samir, please share your repro script when ready.

samir: Will do. ETA ~2h.

cheng: Perf attachments: I dropped flamegraph + perf record in the canary channel (links). Initial flame shows significant time in evicter_lock_holder and in malloc/free during reinserts.

sanjay: Thanks. Next actions: samir repro -> unit test for reinsertion/pager race -> implement per-shard reinserts or lock-free reinserts -> validate memory/regression on canary.

alex: Also add a tiny regression test to CI that runs a mini long-context workload for 30s to catch regressions.

maria: Filing a short RFC for reinsertion redesign; I'll include telemetry schema and rollout plan.

cheng: Thanks all. I'll keep updates in this thread as we get telemetry and repro confirmation. :thumbsup:
